rule: Eyelid lines wrap the eyeball sphere: they look straight only near the centre facing the viewer and curve more and more toward the eyeball's edge, especially in profile and near-profile views.
In three-quarter view the far eye is a little shorter than the near eye, its far corner is blunted, and it sits behind the nose bridge; it must not be pushed out toward the cheek edge.
In three-quarter view the near corner of the near eye keeps nearly its full length and point.
Features drawn each from a different viewing direction make the face look monstrous; all features must follow one head angle.
Common profile errors: dropped ears, sloping forehead, heavy brow, overly deep-set eye, pupil not centred in the iris, nostril pushed back onto the face.
The cheek-to-jaw contour is usually subtle and smooth, especially on women and in frontal views.
